items.when_to_use: Use when everyday terminology groups together items with different purposes, risks, or mechanisms.
items.avoid: Do not merely criticize the label; provide a clear alternative that improves the reader’s ability to reason about the subject.

items.mechanic: Arrange options into layers, beginning with foundational behaviors or conditions and progressing toward more targeted or intensive interventions.
items.when_to_use: Use when choices differ in priority, dependency, or strength of effect.
items.avoid: Do not imply that higher layers are universally superior; explain that later options depend on needs, context, and unresolved gaps.

items.function: Turning advice into a decision framework
items.mechanic: Replace a universal recommendation with a short sequence of diagnostic questions involving need, current outcomes, constraints, affordability, and alternatives.
items.when_to_use: Use when the appropriate choice varies substantially between individuals.
items.avoid: Do not present the questions as a substitute for professional evaluation when safety, diagnosis, or treatment decisions are involved.

items.function: Separating foundational support from targeted effects
items.mechanic: Distinguish broad, gap-filling measures from single-purpose interventions aimed at a defined outcome, then explain why each category may call for a different selection strategy.
items.when_to_use: Use when a product or intervention category contains both general-support and outcome-specific options.
items.avoid: Do not blur prevention, correction of deficiency, enhancement, and treatment into one claim.

items.mechanic: Move from the practical goal to the relevant system, then to the proposed mechanism, and finally to the decision implication.
items.when_to_use: Use when readers need enough biological or technical explanation to understand why an option might help.
items.avoid: Do not introduce mechanistic detail that has no bearing on the decision, and do not treat a plausible mechanism as proof of effectiveness.

items.mechanic: State the strongest version of a skeptical objection, acknowledge the circumstance in which it is valid, and then identify the narrower conditions under which the intervention may still be useful.
items.when_to_use: Use when the topic has polarized opinions or when a simple criticism is partly correct but overgeneralized.
items.avoid: Do not dismiss skeptics rhetorically or neutralize the objection with vague exceptions; specify the relevant conditions and limits.

items.mechanic: Present a case in which the appropriate action is minimal or unnecessary, then contrast it with cases where a need is evident.
items.when_to_use: Use when readers may assume that every person should adopt the same protocol or solution.
items.avoid: Do not use exceptional cases to undermine the general framework; make the decision boundary explicit.

items.mechanic: Briefly restate the hierarchy, categories, or governing principles at transition points so the audience can integrate the accumulated structure before moving to details.
items.when_to_use: Use after a long conceptual section or before shifting from general principles to specific applications.
items.avoid: Do not repeat every example; recap the organizing logic rather than the full preceding discussion.

items.function: Connecting recommendations to constraints and trade-offs
items.mechanic: Evaluate an option not only by its potential benefit but also by cost, convenience, sourcing, timing, interactions, adherence, and opportunity cost.
items.when_to_use: Use when the practical value of an intervention depends on more than efficacy alone.
items.avoid: Do not imply that a more expensive, complex, or concentrated option is automatically higher quality.

items.mechanic: Begin with a topic that appears relevant to a specific subgroup, then broaden its significance to a wider audience by connecting it to shared human experience, general health, or foundational biology.
items.when_to_use: Use when a subject may otherwise seem niche, technical, or personally irrelevant to many readers or listeners.
items.avoid: Do not make universal relevance claims without explaining the bridge between the specialized topic and the broader audience.

items.mechanic: State the major domains, processes, and practical applications that will be covered before introducing detailed explanations.
items.when_to_use: Use at the beginning of a long educational section to establish expectations and reduce uncertainty about where the discussion is going.
items.avoid: Do not provide an exhaustive inventory that overwhelms the audience or promises material the section will not actually address.

items.mechanic: Before presenting terminology or sequential events, explain the central biological or causal problem that the system is solving.
items.when_to_use: Use when the subject contains many stages, specialized terms, or interacting components.
items.avoid: Do not substitute a simplified slogan for the actual mechanism; preserve the core relationships that make later details intelligible.

items.mechanic: Identify terms that are often used interchangeably, distinguish their meanings, and explain why the distinction matters for the argument.
items.when_to_use: Use when public explanations, professional shorthand, or everyday language blur related but nonidentical entities or processes.
items.avoid: Do not introduce distinctions merely to display technical precision; connect each distinction to a practical or explanatory consequence.

items.mechanic: Introduce a concept in plain language, attach the formal term or abbreviation, then reuse the term while linking it to its role in the larger system.
items.when_to_use: Use when teaching specialized vocabulary to a general audience.
items.avoid: Do not introduce several unexplained labels at once, and do not assume that naming a structure is equivalent to explaining it.

items.mechanic: Translate an invisible regulatory process into a familiar feedback system, then map each part of the analogy back to the biological mechanism.
items.when_to_use: Use for feedback loops, thresholds, regulation, inhibition, escalation, or other dynamic relationships that are difficult to visualize.
items.avoid: Do not let the analogy replace the mechanism or imply that the biological system is as simple, linear, or precise as the everyday example.

items.mechanic: Present the general rule, then immediately identify meaningful exceptions, limits, variability, or unresolved causal questions before drawing conclusions.
items.when_to_use: Use when averages, trends, or mechanisms could be mistaken for universal rules or settled explanations.
items.avoid: Do not bury the main conclusion under every possible caveat, and do not treat correlation, animal evidence, or plausible explanations as definitive causation.

items.mechanic: Anticipate the audience's likely inference, explicitly distinguish the supported conclusion from the stronger inference, and redirect attention to the narrower point that the evidence supports.
items.when_to_use: Use when a fact pattern could trigger alarm, stigma, moral judgment, or an overly broad practical conclusion.
items.avoid: Do not introduce sensational interpretations unnecessarily or use reassurance to dismiss legitimate uncertainty.

items.function: Reconstruct the process through periodic recaps
items.mechanic: After several linked steps, briefly restate the sequence in causal order, using the same labels and central objective before advancing to the next stage.
items.when_to_use: Use in long explanations involving multiple organs, signals, stages, or nested processes.
items.avoid: Do not repeat every detail; recap only the relationships that the audience needs in order to follow the next transition.

items.mechanic: Open by naming the subject, connecting it to familiar assumptions, and previewing the practical problems the explanation will address. Frame the discussion as both conceptual and usable.
items.when_to_use: Use at the beginning of an educational piece when the audience may recognize the topic but not understand its deeper significance.
items.avoid: Do not promise outcomes that the explanation cannot support or overload the opening with an exhaustive list of benefits.

items.mechanic: Distinguish the central question from adjacent topics, briefly acknowledge related areas, and state which ones will receive limited or no attention.
items.when_to_use: Use when the subject has multiple branches and readers need to know what the piece will and will not explain.
items.avoid: Avoid introducing so many excluded topics that the scope statement becomes a second outline.

items.function: Building from basic concepts to mechanisms
items.mechanic: Begin with a plain-language definition, establish the relevant system or components, then progressively connect those components to the target behavior or outcome.
items.when_to_use: Use for technical subjects where readers need a mental model before they can evaluate applications.
items.avoid: Avoid introducing specialized terminology before explaining its function or relevance.

items.mechanic: Translate an abstract process into a concrete, familiar model, then map each part of the analogy back to the underlying mechanism. Revisit the analogy as new layers are added.
items.when_to_use: Use when a process involves invisible, dynamic, or multistep changes that are difficult to visualize directly.
items.avoid: Do not let the analogy replace the explanation, and explicitly mark where the comparison stops being exact.

items.mechanic: Explain a process as a sequence of states—starting condition, trigger, rise or change, consequence, recovery, and possible repetition—rather than as a static relationship.
items.when_to_use: Use for behavior, learning, adaptation, motivation, feedback, or any system in which timing affects the result.
items.avoid: Avoid implying that every instance follows an identical sequence or that a simplified timeline captures every variable.

items.mechanic: After describing an internal process, translate it into the subjective experience or observable behavior a person might notice. Then connect that experience back to the mechanism.
items.when_to_use: Use when the audience needs to understand how technical material relates to everyday decisions, habits, or symptoms.
items.avoid: Do not treat a subjective experience as definitive proof of a particular biological process.

items.mechanic: Introduce a typical pattern, then test it against contrasting outcomes such as stronger, weaker, delayed, or reversed responses. Use the contrasts to clarify which variables change the result.
items.when_to_use: Use when a simplified rule could otherwise be mistaken for a universal law.
items.avoid: Avoid presenting unusual cases as representative or using exceptions without explaining what they reveal about the general model.

items.mechanic: Distinguish the signal that drives current behavior from the information-processing system that updates future behavior. Explain how both operate in parallel and interact over time.
items.when_to_use: Use when an explanation involves both short-term motivation and longer-term adaptation.
items.avoid: Avoid collapsing all effects into a single process or suggesting that learning automatically produces consistent behavior.

items.mechanic: Pause after a dense section to restate the model in simpler terms, identify the few elements readers must retain, and then move to the next level of detail.
items.when_to_use: Use in long technical explanations or whenever terminology and causal steps accumulate quickly.
items.avoid: Do not repeat every preceding detail; compress the model around its functional relationships.

items.function: Using an extreme case as a diagnostic
items.mechanic: Examine an unusually strong or clear example first, use it to expose the governing variables, and then return to ordinary cases with a more nuanced interpretation.
items.when_to_use: Use when the core mechanism is easier to see at an extreme and can be transferred back to everyday situations.
items.avoid: State clearly that the extreme case is illustrative, not automatically representative of normal conditions.

items.mechanic: Open by explaining why the subject matters in everyday terms, then immediately distinguish established findings from unresolved causal claims. This creates urgency without overstating certainty.
items.when_to_use: Use for topics that are consequential, emotionally charged, or frequently misrepresented.
items.avoid: Avoid treating prevalence, correlation, plausibility, and causation as interchangeable forms of evidence.

items.mechanic: Present two complementary goals at the outset: accurately understanding the risk and identifying proportionate actions. Explicitly reject both panic and dismissal as incomplete responses.
items.when_to_use: Use when an audience may overreact or disengage because the topic feels overwhelming.
items.avoid: Avoid vague reassurance that undermines the seriousness of the evidence, or alarmist framing that turns information into fear.

items.mechanic: State the major questions the discussion will answer—definition, distribution, possible effects, uncertainty, and practical responses—before developing them in detail.
items.when_to_use: Use in long explanatory pieces with several conceptual and practical sections.
items.avoid: Avoid promising conclusions that the evidence cannot support.

items.function: Define technical categories by threshold and contrast
items.mechanic: Introduce specialized terms through a simple size, scope, or category boundary, then contrast adjacent categories so the audience understands why the distinction matters.
items.when_to_use: Use whenever a subject contains nested technical classifications.
items.avoid: Avoid giving numerical or taxonomic precision without explaining its practical relevance.

items.mechanic: After presenting a potentially alarming observation, add the relevant limitation, uncertainty, or countervailing biological process. Repeat this pattern as the evidence develops.
items.when_to_use: Use when the material includes serious possibilities but incomplete human evidence.
items.avoid: Avoid using reassurance as a rhetorical reset that erases the preceding concern.

items.function: Resolve apparent contradictions by examining measurement
items.mechanic: When two estimates conflict, explain how sampling, instrumentation, detection limits, or analytical methods could produce different results. Use the discrepancy to teach how knowledge changes.
items.when_to_use: Use when new methods revise earlier estimates or when public reporting emphasizes a dramatic number.
items.avoid: Avoid selecting the most dramatic estimate without discussing methodological comparability.

items.mechanic: Explain a general biological or physical mechanism, then connect it to the specific tissues, systems, or outcomes that make the mechanism relevant. Separate plausible pathways from demonstrated effects.
items.when_to_use: Use when audiences need more than a list of findings to understand why they matter.
items.avoid: Avoid presenting a plausible pathway as proof that a real-world outcome occurs.

items.function: Prioritize actions by controllability and proportionality
items.mechanic: Organize recommendations around exposure points that are relatively controllable, potentially meaningful, affordable, and easy to implement. Pair each action with its trade-offs and acknowledge situations where strict avoidance is impractical.
items.when_to_use: Use in science communication that aims to produce behavior change without demanding perfection.
items.avoid: Avoid exhaustive lists with no hierarchy, costly interventions presented as universal obligations, or advice that creates a greater risk than the one being reduced.

items.function: Use delayed callbacks to reinforce understanding
items.mechanic: Briefly flag an important issue, develop the surrounding concepts, and return later to explain it with greater technical clarity. The callback should answer a question created earlier rather than merely repeat information.
items.when_to_use: Use when a complex explanation benefits from conceptual scaffolding.
items.avoid: Avoid callbacks that introduce new terminology without reconnecting it to the original question.

items.mechanic: Open by defining the subject broadly, then specify the main dimensions, time horizons, and outcomes the discussion will cover.
items.when_to_use: Use at the beginning of a complex educational piece to establish scope and give listeners a mental map.
items.avoid: Do not list so many subtopics that the introduction becomes an exhaustive table of contents.

items.function: Convert a large literature into a usable framework
items.mechanic: Acknowledge the size and variety of the evidence base, then explain that the material will be organized by categories, mechanisms, and practical decisions.
items.when_to_use: Use when the audience may feel overwhelmed by numerous studies, variables, or competing protocols.
items.avoid: Do not imply that a simplified framework captures every nuance or that all evidence has identical strength.

items.mechanic: Establish operational definitions for the key categories, including relevant dimensions such as intensity, duration, timing, and outcome type, before comparing them.
items.when_to_use: Use whenever an everyday term covers multiple research-defined interventions or conditions.
items.avoid: Do not rely on familiar labels whose meanings shift across studies.

items.mechanic: After presenting apparently diverse results, identify a shared candidate process that could account for the common pattern, then qualify it as partial rather than complete.
items.when_to_use: Use to move from descriptive evidence toward causal explanation without losing the audience.
items.avoid: Do not treat a plausible mechanism as proven causation or overstate a single explanation.

items.function: Use a counterexample to refine the rule
items.mechanic: Present a seemingly contradictory case—such as a larger dose producing a worse outcome—then explain how timing, threshold, fatigue, or context modifies the general pattern.
items.when_to_use: Use when a simple takeaway risks becoming an overgeneralization.
items.avoid: Do not bury the exception or present it as if it invalidates the broader pattern.

items.mechanic: Show how the same intervention can be positioned before, during, or after a target activity, and connect each option to different scheduling constraints.
items.when_to_use: Use when recommendations depend more on timing and context than on a single universally optimal protocol.
items.avoid: Do not present flexibility as proof that timing never matters.

items.function: Explain mechanisms through a causal chain
items.mechanic: Trace the process from an observable action, through bodily signals or intermediate systems, to a change in the target function.
items.when_to_use: Use when the audience needs enough mechanistic understanding to adapt a recommendation rather than merely follow it.
items.avoid: Do not introduce technical components without explaining their role in the chain.

items.mechanic: Offer a broad, accessible takeaway first, then immediately add the conditions, limits, or exceptions needed for responsible interpretation.
items.when_to_use: Use to maintain clarity while preventing an optimistic summary from being misunderstood as unlimited permission.
items.avoid: Do not let reassurance overshadow important risks, uncertainty, or population differences.

items.mechanic: Periodically restate the main categories, the central mechanism, and the practical implication in a shorter form than the original explanation.
items.when_to_use: Use after a dense section or before transitioning from theory to recommendations.
items.avoid: Do not repeat every supporting detail or introduce new claims during the recap.

items.mechanic: Open by naming a broadly recognized problem, then connect it to an outcome the audience cares about, such as energy, mood, sleep, performance, or recovery.
items.when_to_use: Use at the beginning of an explanatory piece when the subject may initially seem technical or abstract.
items.avoid: Do not inflate importance with unsupported universal claims or imply that one intervention solves every aspect of the problem.

items.mechanic: State one simple rule or contrast that summarizes the main framework, then return to it throughout the explanation.
items.when_to_use: Use when the topic contains many details and the audience needs a compact mental model.
items.avoid: Do not let the simplified rule erase important exceptions, timing differences, or individual variation.

items.mechanic: Identify the audience’s likely default interpretation, acknowledge why it is understandable, and replace it with a broader functional model.
items.when_to_use: Use when a familiar label is accurate in one context but misleading as a complete explanation.
items.avoid: Do not present the correction as an absolute reversal if the original interpretation remains partly valid.

items.mechanic: Explain what a system accomplishes before introducing its components, pathways, terminology, or technical sequence.
items.when_to_use: Use in science, medicine, technology, or policy explanations where specialized vocabulary could otherwise overwhelm the reader.
items.avoid: Do not introduce multiple abbreviations and anatomical or procedural details before establishing their practical purpose.

items.mechanic: Alternate between an abstract summary, a concrete everyday example, and a more detailed mechanistic account; then return to the practical summary.
items.when_to_use: Use when the audience includes both beginners and readers who want technical depth.
items.avoid: Do not switch levels without signaling the change or repeat the same explanation without adding clarity.

items.mechanic: Compare fast and slow components of a response, showing how their different onset and duration produce the observed experience.
items.when_to_use: Use when a phenomenon unfolds in stages or when an intervention’s timing matters.
items.avoid: Do not treat all components as simultaneous when their different timescales are central to the explanation.

items.function: Introduce a model, then test it with edge cases
items.mechanic: Present the typical pattern first, then pose variations that challenge or refine it, such as shorter duration, altered timing, or unusual conditions.
items.when_to_use: Use to prevent a general rule from being mistaken for a rigid schedule or universal outcome.
items.avoid: Do not add edge cases so early that the primary model becomes difficult to understand.

items.function: Derive practical guidance from the mechanism
items.mechanic: Explain why a proposed action should work, identify the relevant time window or condition, and distinguish the foundational action from optional additions.
items.when_to_use: Use when translating explanatory material into a routine, protocol, or decision aid.
items.avoid: Do not provide a checklist without explaining when each step applies or what limitation it has.

items.mechanic: Briefly restate the central framework after each major section, using the recap to show how new details fit into the larger model.
items.when_to_use: Use in long-form explanations with multiple stages, pathways, or qualifications.
items.avoid: Do not recap every sentence; reserve repetition for the governing idea and the implications that depend on it.
